question.text: Activist Cat III funds in India differ from traditional Cat III funds primarily because:

answer.text: They have a LESS diversified portfolio and often hold illiquid investments.
They must have a more diversified portfolio.
They are required to invest 100% in listed securities only.
They are exempt from all concentration limits.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 10.1.4.1: Activist Funds have less diversified portfolios and illiquid investments because they take large stakes to drive operational change. The 10% concentration cap (or 20% for LVFs) binds them to small-mid caps with concentrated positions. The Trap: Option B inverts the rule by claiming a more diversified portfolio. Option C imposes a non-existent 100% listed-securities rule. Option D is false — concentration limits absolutely apply (10% for regular Cat III, 20% for LVF). Note: Activist Cat III funds take concentrated stakes to drive operational change, so portfolios are less diversified and often illiquid, while still being bound by the 10% regular and 20% LVF concentration caps.
